traits: Matt, finely wrinkled cap, up to 20 cm, variable in colour, often mottled green and red
Cream gills, then ochre-yellow with glaucous reflections, then orange; edge lined with red towards the margin
Stem about 12 × 4 cm, dotted, lilac pink at least under the gills, more or less yellowing
Under broadleaves, mostly beeches, in lowlands but mainly in mountains, up to 1,800 m · July to November
safetyNote: Digestive poisonings are reported mostly when it is eaten raw or lightly cooked, on a barbecue for instance: in Italy, a few dozen cases a year; in the Basque Country, over 40 cases in twenty years; in France, 3 grouped cases in 2012, with vomiting 2 hours later. ANSES judged in 2015 that the risk cannot be ruled out, even after cooking; Tox Info Suisse asks for at least 20 minutes of cooking.
